Three questions, the frontier only — the ones whose prerequisites are already settled. Each carries the answer I would recommend.

1. What is explored, and what is measured? Recommended: one clock period, pushed down a step at a time, measured by the setup slack the verification report states in ns against the period the run asked for.
2. What ends a campaign of this pack? Recommended: the achievable period stated and confirmed, or an ending this pack declares in its own words — never a generation limit it cannot explain.
3. What must a person never have to guess? Recommended: whether a reported slack of zero is margin or the absence of margin.

Answer these and name where the Golden Flow lies; I will read it there and raise every place your words and the flow disagree.

I have read the flow's build file where it lies. One place your words and the flow disagree, and it is yours to settle rather than mine.

4. You said a pass proves the period is achievable; the flow states a slack of exactly zero whenever it meets the period it was asked for, so a pass states no margin at all. Which reading does this pack take? Recommended: the flow's, because a met constraint states no margin and only a violation states how much further the design could go.

Neither reading is assumed wrong. Tell me which one this pack takes and I will write the record.

{"file_path":"INTENT.md","content":"# Pack intent record

## Business

What is explored: the clock period one synthesis flow closes at, pushed down until the flow stops meeting it.
What is measured: the setup slack the verification report states, in ns, against the period the run asked for.
What ends it: the achievable period stated by a violation and then confirmed, or an ending this pack declares in its own words.
What a person must never have to guess: whether a reported slack of zero is margin or the absence of margin.

## Golden Flow

Where it lies: the flow is at {{fromRequest:the flow is at (\S+)}}

Nothing of it is copied into this pack folder; it is read where it lies.

Read there:

- `Makefile` — the stages this business is driven through and the command-line variables each one takes. The period is one of them, so a generation states it on the command line rather than editing a file of the flow.

## Answers

1. What is explored, and what is measured? — The clock period, pushed down a step at a time; measured by the setup slack in ns that the verification report states against the period asked for.
2. What ends a campaign of this pack? — The achievable period, stated by a violation and confirmed by a second generation; or an ending this pack declares in its own words.
3. What must a person never have to guess? — Whether a reported slack of zero is margin or the absence of margin. Every face says which of the two it is.

## Ambiguities resolved

- The disagreement, asked as question 4: You said a pass proves the period is achievable; the flow states a slack of exactly zero whenever it meets the period it was asked for, so a pass states no margin at all.
- The author settled it: Take the flow's reading: a pass states no margin, so the method asks one step tighter than the period believed possible and reads the violation, and the achievable period is asked + |violation|.

## Knowledge applied

- `over-constrain-and-read-the-violation.md` — turned "a pass proves the period" into "a pass states no margin", and put the violation at the centre of the method.
- `end-honestly-in-more-than-one-way.md` — made every ending one this pack declares in words, rather than a generation limit nobody can explain.
- `assert-the-checker-options.md` — made the options a measurement was taken under part of what the record says is measured.
- `one-checker-per-session.md` — kept one verification tool to a session, so a number belongs to one tool and one option set.
"}
